title: Niyama
description: Cultivate inner purity and contentment through the five personal observances that create a stable environment for spiritual growth.

sutra.meaning: Yama (moral injunctions), Niyama (observances), Āsana (posture), Prāṇāyāma (regulation of breath), Pratyāhāra (withholding of senses), Dhāraṇā (fixity of attention), Dhyāna (meditation), and Samādhi (absorption of consciousness in the self) are the eight accessories (limbs) of Yoga

sections.practice: attempt to take up one new practice or change in lifestyle in accordance with yamas and niyamas

sutra.meaning: Cleanliness, contentment, discipline, self-study, surrender, these fixed observances refine inner life.

sections.insight: There is always scope for improvement in following all of these Niyamas
sections.reflectionPrompt: Which one needs special attention from me?
sections.practice: Focus on one at a time. Which one is particularly challenging for me.
sections.journalPrompt: What changes was I inspired to make in my life?

sutra.meaning: There may be doubts about the claims of yoga made in this text of Sri Patanjali and made in other yoga books, however one should cast these doubts aside and practice. When the doubts arise, one should ignore the doubtful ideas and push ahead with practice.

sections.insight: In the case of the annoyance produced by doubts, one should conceive of what is opposite.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do doubts arise in me regarding the sutras?
sections.practice: Dont let doubts affect your practice.
sections.journalPrompt: What doubts I have encountered during my practices.

sutra.meaning: Purity leads to respect for body and mind

sections.reflectionPrompt: Negative and unclean thoughts have an impact on how you feel and see yourself.

sutra.meaning: Purification of the psyche results in benevolence, the ability of one pointed attention, control of  sensual energy, awareness of the consciousness and ability of abstract meditation.

sections.insight: When the body is cleansed, the mind purified and the senses controlled , joyful awareness required to realize the inner self also comes.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Do I maintain hygiene and feel clean?
sections.practice: Maintain cleanliness in body and mind.
sections.journalPrompt: Did I make any lifestyle changes.

sutra.meaning: From contentment, the very best in happiness is obtained.

sections.journalPrompt: What did I have enough of?

sutra.meaning: Austerity, resulting in the elimination of impurity produces perfection of the body and sensual energy.

sections.insight: Self-discipline (tapas) burns away impurities and kindles the sparks of Divinity.
sections.reflectionPrompt: Is maintaining discipline a problem for me.
sections.practice: Make a note of areas of your life which need you to be disciplined. Can you commit to yourself to make an effort in the area/s.
sections.journalPrompt: Did the commitment seem like a burden or serve as an inspiration.

sutra.meaning: From study of our own psyche, comes intimate contact with the cherished divine being.

sections.insight: asana and pranayama are integral to connecting awareness of the body with core and vice versa
sections.reflectionPrompt: Can I commit to my daily practice or kriya
sections.practice: Practice asana and pranayam with complete focus inward.
sections.journalPrompt: is yoga practice enjoyable or painful for me

sutra.meaning: From  profound  meditation upon the Divine comes the perfection of continuous effortless linkage of the attention to that Divinity.

sections.insight: The power of samadhi comes to him who takes refuge in the Divine.
sections.reflectionPrompt: surrender to God brings perfection in samadhi. Can I surrender to the Divine?
sections.practice: sit for meditation with the intention of total surrender
